items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are mostly clear and the public methods have one-line docs. But the new Batch fields (commitSync, walSyncWG, applyStart...) have no comments, and the inline goroutine in prepare() that does the WG juggling has no comment explaining it. durabilityManager fields are only partly documented.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: recordJobAllocated is dead code. waitForDurability repeats its seq==0 and highestDurableSeqNum checks in the ctx.Done branch, and waitForJobDurability does the same. A ~35-line goroutine is inlined in prepare(), and the logic is split between batch.go, commit.go and db.go instead of living behind a clean onDurable hook.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: `endSeq := info.SeqNum + base.SeqNum(info.KeyCount)` is off by one: the durable seq should be SeqNum+Count-1. Spawning a goroutine per sync commit lets notifications arrive out of order. Durations are clamped to 1ns. Errors are propagated rather than swallowed, and the bounds are named consts.

items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
items.evidence: The new APIs are additive. However, every Sync commit now runs allocateJobID() under a mutex and spawns a goroutine (`go func(b *Batch, noSyncWait bool)`) even when BatchDurable is unset. The NoSyncWait path is rerouted through walSyncWG and that goroutine, and the callback also fires for NoSyncWait commits.
